title.suggested: Tom Kelly and Tom Allen differ on the Sullivan-Corbett fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Kelly backed Corbett after his win over Sullivan, while Tom Allen said Sullivan lost on condition and, properly trained, could still beat Corbett.

metadata.notes: Database title "Verying Views" is a typo; database summary wrongly says 1899 (paper is 1892-09-13).

facts.fact: Allen said Sullivan lost to Corbett because he was out of condition and overweight, and that he did not rate Corbett as Sullivan's superior; he allowed Corbett won squarely and is skillful
facts.quote: It was all a question of condition. Sullivan was unfit to enter the ring; he was away over-weight and unable to cope with a man of Corbett's agility. I don't recognize Corbett as Sullivan's superior.

notes: Title is a headline; Allen section is the second half. Focus was blank in the database.
